authority: Ministry of Food Processing Industries / Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana
interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: MoFPI guidelines, circulars, scheme pages, official FAQs, the current MoFPI archive and the SAMPADA handoff are the primary sources. PMKSY components remain separate records. Project ceilings, assistance rates and programme-level status are not applicant entitlements; live EOIs and current guideline versions must control publication.

records.sourceAnchor: Component-specific cold-chain/value-addition assistance, staged project support, current irradiation EOI and separate facility-registration dependencies
observations: The current MoFPI source set identifies the Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure component and a revised guideline dated 22 May 2025. The exact eligible-cost, facility, applicant, rate and release provisions must be extracted from that version before publication.

The current Cold Chain circular list shows a multiproduct food irradiation EOI dated 20 May 2026 and an extension notice dated 31 August 2026. The official extension is to 17:00 on 30 September 2026 and applies only to that specified irradiation EOI, not to every cold-chain or value-addition proposal.

The current circular list also shows a July 2026 notice concerning compulsory WDRA registration of cold-storage facilities created under the Cold Chain scheme. This is a separate facility/compliance dependency and must not be silently treated as satisfied by the PMKSY grant application.

This is project-level grant-in-aid subject to EOI selection, eligible project cost, promoter/finance evidence, technical and statutory readiness, milestones and staged release. A project ceiling or assistance percentage is not a guaranteed payment to an individual business.

The official PMKSY policy material describes a demand-driven EOI route and distinguishes PMKSY component schemes. Any standalone cold-storage, godown, logistics or transportation boundary must be reconciled against the current guideline and exact project configuration before recommendation.

SAMPADA is the official handoff route identified in the seed. UdyamVeda may prepare a project-readiness dossier and link the applicant to the official route, but must not submit credentials, guarantee approval or represent MoFPI.

The 2026 deadline is time-sensitive and should become stale quickly if not reverified. The recommendation must show the exact EOI scope, last verification date and remaining document/technical effort rather than a generic cold-chain deadline.
reviewFollowUps: Extract and verify the 22 May 2025 guideline sections for eligible entities, facilities, project cost, rates, ceiling, promoter contribution, term loan, release milestones and clawback/monitoring conditions.
Confirm that the 20 May 2026 irradiation EOI remains open and that the 30 September 2026 17:00 deadline is still applicable to the applicant's exact proposal type.
Reconcile the July 2026 WDRA registration requirement, food-safety, pollution-control, local and other facility permissions with the proposed site and facility.
Confirm whether the project is integrated and eligible rather than a standalone cold storage, godown, logistics or transport proposal outside the current component rules.
Verify current SAMPADA portal fields, documents, fee instructions, signatory requirements, project appraisal and staged-release evidence.
Check amendments, corrigenda, current fund availability, approved-project interactions and any duplicate-assistance restrictions before publication.
Obtain a human reviewer decision; keep the record review-gated and do not publish the 30 September 2026 date as a general PMKSY deadline.

records.sourceAnchor: New, modernised or expanded food-processing capacity, project-level grant, 2025 guideline/EOI history and current-window uncertainty
observations: MoFPI publishes CEFPPC/Unit Scheme guidelines dated 22 January 2025 and lists a 27 January 2025 EOI with an extension dated 28 March 2025. These establish the component route and historical call context, not a currently open application window in September 2026.

The current MoFPI archive displays the 2025 CEFPPC EOI, extension, FAQ, guidelines and approved-project status notices. No newer open CEFPPC EOI was identified in the current archive check; this must be confirmed by a reviewer before the record is labelled open or actionable.

The route is for project-level creation, expansion or modernisation of eligible food-processing and preservation capacity. The draft ceiling and assistance rates remain subject to the current guideline's eligible-cost, category, applicant, finance and EOI conditions.

A project ceiling is not an assured individual grant, and CEFPPC must remain separate from PMFME's micro-enterprise route. Existing-unit expansion requires baseline/capacity evidence and cannot be inferred from a business profile alone.

The official application path is EOI-based with SAMPADA handoff, technical/financial appraisal and milestone/utilization review. UdyamVeda can prepare and explain the dossier but cannot guarantee selection or file as the applicant.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm whether a new CEFPPC EOI is open, paused, closed or superseded after the 2025 EOI and extension; do not infer active status from the scheme page alone.

Extract the 22 January 2025 guideline sections for eligible entities, sectors, unit/expansion conditions, project-cost ceiling, assistance rate, promoter contribution, term loan and release milestones.
Verify the applicant's new-unit or expansion status, baseline capacity, site, plant and machinery, food-safety and statutory permissions.
Reconcile the EOI scope for units outside Mega Food Parks/APCs and the January 2025 withdrawal notice for the older 2023 EOI.
Verify SAMPADA application fields, documents, fees, appraisal route, reporting and any current fund or duplicate-assistance restrictions.
Keep the record review-gated until current window evidence and the exact eligible-cost calculation are anchored to the applicable version.

records.sourceAnchor: Cluster/common infrastructure, producer-processor-market linkage, project-level grant and 2025 EOI history
observations: MoFPI lists operational APC guidelines dated 25 April 2025. The current guideline page and archive also show a 14 May 2025 APC EOI and a 1 July 2025 FAQ, so the route is a cluster/common-infrastructure project route rather than an ordinary individual-unit subsidy.

The official policy answer describes PMKSY as demand-driven with applications invited through EOI and lists APC, Integrated Cold Chain and CEFPPC as separate component schemes. A historical EOI or approved-project list is not evidence that a new APC EOI is open now.

The draft ceiling and assistance rates are project-level amounts subject to eligible-cost, cluster structure, applicant/SPV, producer/processor linkage, finance, statutory and milestone conditions. They must not be displayed as a guaranteed amount for one business.

The APC scope covers common enabling and core processing infrastructure that links producers or farmers with processors and markets. A standalone unit without a documented cluster/common-infrastructure rationale should not receive an APC recommendation.
APC must remain separate from CEFPPC, PMFME and Cold Chain. The official application handoff is through the applicable MoFPI/SAMPADA route, with project appraisal and utilization/completion evidence.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm whether a current APC EOI is open, paused, closed or superseded after the 14 May 2025 call; do not use the 2025 EOI date as a current deadline.
Extract the 25 April 2025 guideline sections for cluster area, common enabling/core facilities, applicant/SPV structure, eligible cost, grant ceiling, promoter contribution and milestones.
Verify producer, processor and market linkages, site/utilities, finance, implementation structure and all applicable statutory permissions.
Check the 1 July 2025 FAQ, corrigenda, approved-project notices and any later amendment or duplicate-assistance restrictions.
Verify current SAMPADA fields, document formats, appraisal authority, fee instructions, reporting and completion evidence.
Keep the record review-gated until current EOI evidence and the project's common-infrastructure fit are independently confirmed.

publicationGuard.reason: Official MoFPI sources confirm the three distinct PMKSY component routes and the current irradiation extension, but current EOI status, exact eligible-cost treatment, project/applicant structure, facility dependencies, amendments, fund availability and live portal acceptance require human reconciliation. All records stay review-gated.
